Done. The plan at `out/T1/plan.yaml` ran successfully on the second execution and wrote `out/T1/model.safetensors`.

What the plan does:
- Deletes all tensors of blocks 2, 6, 10, 14 with one anchored regex, then asserts none remain.
- Renumbers the surviving blocks with ten `move` transforms in ascending source order, so each destination index is already vacant and no collision is possible.
- Asserts the required checks: no block index 12 or higher exists, exactly 12 query_key_value weights, 180 block tensors, 184 tensors total, and the 4 non-block tensors present.

Independent check of the written file confirms 184 tensors with block indices 0 through 11.

Executions: 2. The first failed at plan parse time because I wrote `inputs` as a name/path mapping instead of the `alias::path` string form the README documents. No output was written by that attempt. `out/T1/REPORT.md` records this along with the pitfalls.
